speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for coming in today regarding your neck swelling. To help me understand your condition better, how long have you noticed this lump, and has it been growing?

Have you experienced any pain, difficulty swallowing, or changes in your voice?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Colon Cancer to the Neck (Likely Cervical Lymph Nodes)

Given your history of colon cancer and the new, painless, progressively enlarging mass on the nape of your neck, I am highly concerned for metastatic disease. I need to confirm this with imaging and a biopsy. REQUEST TEST: CT Neck with Contrast; REQUEST TEST: Fine Needle Aspiration Biopsy of the neck mass.
